<div class="tbx p-advice">
<div class="head"><h1>Advice and MSE</h1><span class="badge">Draft</span>
<p class="lead">An accepted assessment becomes scientific advice in three steps: stock status is compared with reference points, results are set out in a standard advice format, and, where a harvest control rule or technical measure needs testing, simplified management strategy evaluation (MSE) shows how options perform before they are adopted.</p>
<div class="jump"><span class="label" style="margin:0">On this page</span><a href="#route">From assessment to advice</a><a href="#which">Choosing a route</a><a href="#tools">Tools</a><a href="#planned">Planned content</a></div></div>
<div class="band"><section id="route"><h2>From assessment to advice</h2><p class="sub">Part of workstream 3. The three steps apply to results from any FAO tool, so advice stays comparable across methods and stocks.</p><div class="stg"><div class="fs" style="--c:#2b6fd6"><small>Step 1</small><b>Compare status with reference points</b><p>An accepted assessment gives biomass and fishing mortality, which are compared with reference points such as B<sub>lim</sub> and proxies for F<sub>MSY</sub> to show where the stock stands.</p></div><div class="ar">→</div><div class="fs" style="--c:#0f766e"><small>Step 2</small><b>Present advice in a standard format</b><p>Results are set out in a consistent set of plots and tables, whichever assessment method produced them, so managers see comparable advice across stocks.</p></div><div class="ar">→</div><div class="fs" style="--c:#8e44ad"><small>Step 3</small><b>Test rules and measures where needed</b><p>Where a harvest control rule or technical measure must be chosen, simplified management strategy evaluation shows how options perform against risk, yield, and stability before adoption.</p></div></div></section></div>
<div class="band white"><section id="which"><h2>Choosing a route</h2><p class="sub">The route depends on the question being asked, because a stock assessment alone does not test a rule or compare management options.</p><table class="rt"><tr><th>Question</th><th>Route</th><th>Tool</th><th>Result</th></tr><tr><td>How does the stock compare with reference points, and what does that imply for advice?</td><td>Advice translation</td><td><a href="#flref">FLRef</a></td><td>Reference points, status plots, advice tables</td></tr><tr><td>Will a harvest control rule meet objectives for risk, yield, and stability?</td><td>Formal MSE</td><td><a href="#flrmse">FLR mse</a></td><td>Performance of rules against an operating model</td></tr><tr><td>Which technical measure (size limit, effort cap, closure, or catch limit) suits the fishery?</td><td>Participatory screening</td><td><a href="#fpat">FPAT App</a></td><td>Projected catch and abundance by measure</td></tr><tr><td>How should a mixed fishery with several species and one effort cap be handled?</td><td>Multispecies methods</td><td><a href="#mmsyfm">mmsyFM</a> with <a href="#msmse">MSMSE</a> or <a href="#flrmse">FLR mse</a></td><td>Multispecies reference points, effort caps, and rule performance</td></tr></table></section></div>
<div class="band"><section id="tools"><h2>Tools for advice and MSE</h2><p class="sub">Five tools cover the steps, from translating an assessment into advice to quick screening of measures and formal testing of harvest control rules, with multispecies tools for mixed fisheries. Each box sets out what the tool does, the data it needs, what it produces, cautions, and links to code and materials.</p><div class="tools tools3"><div class="tool" id="flref" style="--c:#1f5fa8;--tint:#eef4fb"><div class="th"><h3>FLRef</h3><span class="tag">R package</span></div><div class="tb"><p class="obj">Turns accepted assessments from SPiCT, JABBA, and FLicc into reference points and a standard set of advice plots and tables, so that results from different methods reach managers in one consistent format, whichever model produced them.</p><dl></dl><h5>Data needed</h5><ul class="bl"><li>Output of an accepted assessment from SPiCT, JABBA, or FLicc</li><li>Converter function for that tool: <b>spict2FLStockR()</b>, <b>jabba2FLStockR()</b>, or <b>flicc2FLStockR()</b></li></ul><h5>Outputs</h5><ul class="bl"><li>Reference points</li><li>Stock status plots from <b>plotAdvice()</b></li><li>Advice tables</li><li>Harvest control rule summaries</li></ul><h5>How to use the outputs</h5><ul class="bl"><li>Compare stock status with reference points</li><li>Present advice in one standard format across stocks and methods</li><li>Pass results to an MSE when a rule or measure must be tested</li></ul><h5>Use with care</h5><div class="wn"><b>Testing rules.</b> An assessment alone does not test a harvest control rule. Use it as the estimation model within an MSE.</div><div class="wn"><b>Technical measures.</b> Express advice as effort, size, or area rather than catch limits, and test options in simulation.</div><div class="wn"><b>Comparing options.</b> Condition an operating model and compare options in simulation.</div><div class="wn"><b>Still to complete.</b> Diagnostics and sensitivities, and case studies, are to be added.</div><div class="sp"></div><div class="links"><a class="btn" href="https://github.com/Henning-Winker/FLRef" target="_blank">Code on GitHub &#8599;</a><a class="lk" href="flref.qmd" target="_blank">Toolbox entry page <span>&#8594;</span></a><a class="lk off">Standard advice formats <i>To be added</i></a><a class="lk off">Reference-point conventions <i>To be added</i></a></div></div></div><div class="tool" id="flrmse" style="--c:#6b4fa0;--tint:#f4f0fa"><div class="th"><h3>FLR mse</h3><span class="tag">R package</span></div><div class="tb"><p class="obj">Tests harvest control rules and management procedures against an operating model in closed-loop simulation, showing how each performs for risk, yield, and stability before a rule is adopted. It covers simplified and full MSE.</p><dl></dl><h5>Data needed</h5><ul class="bl"><li>An operating model for the stock and fishery</li><li>An estimation model, for example an assessment such as FLicc through <b>flicc.sa()</b></li><li>Candidate harvest control rules or management procedures</li></ul><h5>Outputs</h5><ul class="bl"><li>Performance of each rule against risk, yield, and stability</li><li>Comparison of management procedures under the same operating model</li></ul><h5>How to use the outputs</h5><ul class="bl"><li>Choose between rules by weighing risk, yield, and stability</li><li>Test a rule before adoption</li><li>Follow quick screening with FPAT App by formal testing of a chosen rule</li></ul><h5>Use with care</h5><div class="wn"><b>Testing rules.</b> A fitted assessment does not test a rule. Use it as the estimation model within an MSE.</div><div class="wn"><b>Comparing options.</b> Condition an operating model and compare options in simulation. Use FPAT App for quick screening and FLR mse for rule testing.</div><div class="wn"><b>Still to complete.</b> Data template, key parameters, assumptions, sensitivity demos, and case studies are to be added.</div><div class="sp"></div><div class="links"><a class="lk" href="mse.qmd" target="_blank">Toolbox entry page <span>&#8594;</span></a><a class="lk off">Kell et al. (2007) paper <i>Link to add</i></a><a class="lk off">Training materials <i>To be added</i></a><a class="lk off">Sensitivity demos <i>To be added</i></a></div></div></div><div class="tool" id="fpat" style="--c:#0f7c86;--tint:#eef8f8"><div class="th"><h3>FPAT App</h3><span class="tag">Shiny app</span></div><div class="tb"><p class="obj">Builds an operating model from the Fisheries Performance Assessment Toolkit (FPAT) workbook and projects how catch limits, effort limits, size limits, or closures might change abundance and catch. It suits quick, participatory screening when the question is which measure to use rather than how much to catch.</p><dl></dl><h5>Data needed</h5><ul class="bl"><li>Catch history, with incomplete catches corrected first</li><li>Core life-history parameters</li><li>Answers to ten app questions on completeness, discards, closures, feasibility, and index behaviour</li><li>A standardised index (recommended), for example from cpueTargeting</li><li>Fishery treated as one aggregate fleet</li></ul><h5>Outputs</h5><ul class="bl"><li>Projected catch and abundance for each procedure</li><li>Trade-off plots</li><li>Procedures compared: current catch, current effort, two size limits, two length-targeting rules, two index-targeting rules, and area closures</li></ul><h5>How to use the outputs</h5><p style="margin:0 0 6px;font-size:17px;line-height:1.45">The app is step 2 of the FPAT cycle (FAO Technical Paper 737), used in workshops of about three days with 4 to 12 participants.</p><ol class="cy"><li><span><b>Benchmark.</b> Fishery performance indicators and a governance review show where a fishery underperforms and which measures are enforceable.</span></li><li class="me"><span><b>Plan.</b> This app compares candidate measures in simulation.</span></li><li><span><b>Decide.</b> Stakeholders weigh the trade-offs and choose.</span></li><li><span><b>Monitor and repeat.</b> Performance is reassessed as data improve.</span></li></ol><h5>Use with care</h5><div class="wn"><b>Screening only.</b> The app gives no stand-alone catch advice. Use FLR mse for formal rule testing.</div><div class="wn"><b>Mixed fisheries.</b> Use mmsyFM or MSMSE instead. A multispecies trawl fishery with a joint effort cap is an unsuitable case, and a single-species, single-gear coastal fishery a suitable one.</div><div class="wn"><b>Sensitivities.</b> Results depend on starting depletion (fixed at 1), natural mortality and steepness, reporting bias, effort creep, and index behaviour.</div><div class="wn"><b>Software status.</b> The R package (v0.2.0, on openMSE) was last updated in September 2023. Confirm availability of the hosted app with Blue Matter Science before using it in training.</div><div class="sp"></div><div class="links"><a class="lk off">Open FPAT App <i>Hosted app to confirm</i></a><a class="lk" href="fpat.qmd" target="_blank">Toolbox entry page <span>&#8594;</span></a><a class="lk off">FAO Technical Paper 737 <i>In press</i></a><a class="lk off">Sensitivity demos <i>To be added</i></a></div></div></div><div class="tool" id="mmsyfm" style="--c:#b0386b;--tint:#fbf0f5"><div class="th"><h3>mmsyFM</h3><span class="tag">R package</span></div><div class="tb"><p class="obj">Estimates multispecies reference points and effort caps for mixed fisheries in which several interacting species are caught together, so that a joint effort limit does not overexploit the weakest stock.</p><dl></dl><h5>Data needed</h5><ul class="bl"><li>To be added</li></ul><h5>Outputs</h5><ul class="bl"><li>Multispecies reference points</li><li>Effort caps for mixed fisheries</li></ul><h5>How to use the outputs</h5><ul class="bl"><li>Set a joint effort cap for a mixed fishery</li><li>Pass multispecies reference points to an MSE where a rule must be tested</li></ul><h5>Use with care</h5><div class="wn"><b>Still to complete.</b> Data needed, assumptions, key parameters, sensitivity demos, and case studies are to be added.</div><div class="wn"><b>Placement.</b> Also shown on the assessment methods figure. Confirm whether it sits there, here, or both.</div><div class="sp"></div><div class="links"><a class="lk off">Code on GitHub <i>Link to add</i></a><a class="lk off">Training materials <i>To be added</i></a></div></div></div><div class="tool" id="msmse" style="--c:#b45309;--tint:#fdf5ec"><div class="th"><h3>MSMSE</h3><span class="tag">R package</span></div><div class="tb"><p class="obj">Tests harvest control rules and management procedures for several interacting species in closed-loop simulation, as the multispecies counterpart of single-species MSE.</p><dl></dl><h5>Data needed</h5><ul class="bl"><li>To be added</li></ul><h5>Outputs</h5><ul class="bl"><li>Performance of rules and procedures for each species and for the fishery as a whole</li></ul><h5>How to use the outputs</h5><ul class="bl"><li>Compare management procedures under multispecies interactions</li><li>Weigh trade-offs among species before a rule is adopted</li></ul><h5>Use with care</h5><div class="wn"><b>Still to complete.</b> Objective, data needed, outputs, assumptions, sensitivity demos, and case studies are to be confirmed and added.</div><div class="wn"><b>Placement.</b> Confirm how its role differs from FLR mse and mmsyFM.</div><div class="sp"></div><div class="links"><a class="lk off">Code on GitHub <i>Link to add</i></a><a class="lk off">Training materials <i>To be added</i></a></div></div></div></div></section></div>
<div class="band white"><section id="planned"><h2>Planned content</h2><p class="sub">Content still to be written for this section, as listed in the current catalogue: standard advice formats, reference-point conventions for data-limited stocks (such as B<sub>lim</sub> and F<sub>MSY</sub> proxies), and guidance on capacity and effort limits where catch limits are not practical.</p>
